headline: Asia's night futures bounce modestly after Wall Street's rebound, with Seoul's rate decision due as US markets go dark for Thanksgiving

findings.headline: Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei night futures recovered only a sliver of Wednesday's chip rout
findings.body: Osaka's night session in Nikkei futures settled 250 yen higher at 57,290, and CME Nikkei futures were still slightly bid after that close. KOSPI 200 night futures finished 0.35% higher at 727.30 after swinging from a low of 688.80 during the US sell-off, while TAIEX night futures rose 274 points and TSMC futures gained 13 Taiwan dollars. That is a modest bid into this morning's cash open, not a retracement of Wednesday's heavy losses in Korea and Taiwan, and with US cash markets shut for Thanksgiving it is the first real test of whether Wall Street's late rotation — cyclicals leading, chips still lagging — carries into Asia on thin holiday liquidity.

findings.headline: US futures are little changed after the close, and no late earnings recast the session
findings.body: After Wednesday's cash close, Dow futures were little changed and S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were only slightly softer, leaving the rebound intact into the holiday. The after-hours tape added no fresh earnings shock to change that picture; Tuesday night's reports from HP and Dell had already been absorbed in Wednesday's cash session. US stocks and bonds stay shut on Thursday, with a short session on Friday, so Asia and Europe will have to trade the rebound without a New York lead.

sources.label: IBD: Dow futures little changed after hours; S&P and Nasdaq futures slightly softer

findings.headline: The Bank of Korea decision, and a hawkish BoJ voice, land in a holiday-thin session
findings.body: Around 02:00 Zurich, the Bank of Korea is due to announce its last policy decision of 2026, with a Reuters poll finding 32 of 34 economists expect a quarter-point rise to 3.25% after a pause in October, plus updated forecasts. At the same hour, Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura, a known hawk, speaks in Yamanashi; a mid-December BoJ hike is already the base case, so the risk is what he says about the path after that. In a session with no US cash market, either headline can move the won and the yen more than usual.

view: Our view: Night-session bids in Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei are a tentative vote that Wednesday's US rebound can travel, but they only claw back a sliver of the chip-led damage, and a holiday-thin Thursday can swing hard on the Bank of Korea or a hawkish line from Tamura. Oil is still holding a Gulf risk premium into the 29 November OPEC+ meeting, with no fresh official word from Riyadh overnight on Ras Tanura.
